extracted.intended_audience: U.S. consumers who purchased (or considered purchasing) recent iPhone models and want to know class-action settlement eligibility
extracted.subtask_description: Determine whether a consumer is part of the proposed $250M Apple class-action settlement and what payment they might receive, based on device, purchase date, and procedural requirements. Covers who is included, payout amounts, and next steps for claims and court approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement class membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement class, or the group eligible for payment, includes anyone in the United States who purchased an eligible device during a certain time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both sides agreed to the $250M settlement but a court must approve the agreement before payments can be distributed; a court hearing is scheduled for June. Membership requires meeting the device, time-period, and jurisdictional criteria described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible devices: iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 15 Pro, or iPhone 15 Pro Max.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only purchasers of the explicitly listed models are included in the settlement class; other models are not listed as eligible in the filings referenced by the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period of purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Time period of purchase: June 10, 2024 to March 29, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be in the settlement class a purchase must have occurred within these inclusive dates; purchases outside this window are not covered by the described settlement class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional requirement (U.S. purchasers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement class includes anyone in the United States who purchased an eligible device during the specified time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-U.S. purchasers are not covered by this settlement class as described in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment amount per eligible device
rubrics_metrics.description: If the settlement is approved, eligible people are slated to get a payout of $25 per eligible device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline payout reported in the filings; the actual amount will depend on final approval and claim counts (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential increase to payment depending on claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the number of approved claims, that total could increase to $95 per device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The per-device payout may rise from the baseline $25 up to $95 if the number of approved claims is low enough to allow a larger per-claim distribution from the $250M fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for court approval before distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: A court must approve the settlement agreement before payments can be sent to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement is subject to judicial approval; a hearing was scheduled for June (per the article). Only after approval will the settlement administrator provide claim-filing details and distributions occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim submission/process expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: A settlement administrator website — where more details on submitting claims will be provided — is expected soon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumers will likely need to submit claims through the settlement administrator once the court approves the settlement; the article indicates claim filing details and forms will be posted on that site.
